q: Which way of reading the sentence ‘She raced to the finish line.’ shows the best expression?
o: Read all words quickly with the same tone.
Pause slightly after ‘She’ then read the rest quickly.
Read with a lively voice and emphasize the word ‘raced’.
a: Read with a lively voice and emphasize the word ‘raced’.
e: Emphasizing ‘raced’ and using a lively pace matches the meaning and shows appropriate prosody.

q: Which sentence is the best opening sentence for a 1-minute oral report about school gardens?
o: Today I will tell you three ways school gardens help students learn about science.
a: Today I will tell you three ways school gardens help students learn about science.
e: This sentence previews the structure (three ways) and helps listeners follow the presentation.

q: Choose the sentence that uses quotation marks correctly.
e: Quotation marks surround the quoted words and the comma is inside the quotes before the attribution.

q: The word ‘unhappy’ contains the prefix ‘un-’. What does this prefix most likely mean?
e: The prefix ‘un-’ usually means ‘not’, so ‘unhappy’ means ‘not happy’.

q: Which word shows the meaning of the suffix ‘-ful’?
e: The suffix ‘-ful’ means ‘full of’, so ‘joyful’ means full of joy.

q: Which is the strongest topic sentence for a paragraph about school gardens?
o: School gardens can help students learn about plants and responsibility.
I saw a garden behind the school.
There are many different plants in gardens.
a: School gardens can help students learn about plants and responsibility.
e: This sentence states a clear topic and gives reasons that can be developed in the paragraph.

q:
Passage: The playground was empty, and dark clouds gathered overhead. Jordan zipped his coat and hurried home.
What can the reader infer from the passage?
o: Jordan had a party to attend.
e: Dark clouds and hurrying home suggest that rain is likely, so the inference is that it might start to rain.

q:
Passage: Nia practiced the violin every morning. When she made a mistake, she marked the measure and tried it again.
Which detail best shows Nia is a careful musician?
o: She marked the measure when she made a mistake.
a: She marked the measure when she made a mistake.
e: Marking a measure and trying again shows careful practice and attention to improvement.

q:
Text A: Solar panels use sunlight to make electricity.
Text B: Wind turbines use moving air to make electricity.
Which sentence compares the two texts?
o: Both describe ways to make electricity from natural resources.
Only solar panels can make electricity at night.
Wind turbines use sunlight to work.
Both need water to make electricity.
a: Both describe ways to make electricity from natural resources.
e: Both texts explain renewable methods (sunlight, wind) to produce electricity from natural resources.
